observations.analysis: The captured SBCL manual distinguishes executable/core/startup state and implementation-sensitive FASL compatibility; ASDF provides system-resolution and output configuration, not a dependency lock. Document11 correctly imposes digest-bound toolchain/source/dependency/core provenance as binding policy and rejects saved development cores. Lease/owner/generation correlations are the existing neutral protocol requirements, not claims made by the manuals. Online SBCL2.6.9 documentation does not establish local2.2.9 behavior.

CLHS macroexpand obtains an expansion function and calls the macroexpand hook with it; print-object is a generic function with user-defined methods. Inspect interaction and side effects are implementation-dependent and may modify inspected structures. These sources justify treating observation as potential execution. Document11 conservatively extends ownership/lease/generation and serialization rules to it. Shared editor clients are a possible shared-image arrangement, not an observed SLY deployment or an isolation proof.

CLHS load executes encountered forms sequentially. Top-level processing expands macros and evaluates relevant eval-when bodies; defining macros can have compile-time effects whose visibility varies. Compile-file returns separate pathname, warnings-p and failure-p values. Earlier arbitrary effects need not roll back on a later error, so the conservative image_consistent:false and reconstruction policy is justified. Document11 does not equate a produced pathname with success or claim all compile effects become runtime definitions.

Handler-bind handlers run in the signaling dynamic contour; handler-case transfers and unwinds before its selected clause. Restart-case/restart-bind establish context-dependent restarts and report callbacks, supporting capture while applicable and descriptions rather than persistent invocable restart objects. SBCL invoke-debugger-hook applies at debugger entry, including break, rather than every signaled condition. CLHS printer controls depend on method cooperation and do not bound arbitrary callback execution. Independent byte/time budgets and trusted fallback are conservative requirements.

CLHS defvar preserves an already bound value. Explicit fmakunbound/remove-method operations remove live definitions; source omission alone is not either operation. Defconstant changed-value consequences and defstruct redefinition consequences are undefined under CLHS; reconstruction is a consumer policy, not a claim of a universal syntactic prohibition. Class redefinition retains class/object identity and updates instances at implementation-dependent times; generated old accessors are removed, whereas arbitrary user methods need explicit removal. The binding keeps those distinctions.

Captured SBCL Special Variables states shared global values, thread-local bindings, and no inheritance of parent dynamic bindings. Explicit worker context bindings follow; synchronization of a shared value is a separate concern. The worker/resource accounting and ownership-transfer policy adds governance constraints without claiming that lexical parent let provides child dynamic bindings or that finished workers certify image consistency.

SBCL join-thread times out the caller wait; depending on :default it returns a timeout indication or signals join-thread-error. It does not terminate the target. Document11 avoids depending on a specific return convention and retains busy/uncertain status. Interrupt-thread is asynchronous and introduces reentrancy and unwind-protect cleanup hazards; terminate-thread also causes asynchronous unwind. Correlated observed stopping and separate consistency assessment are binding requirements; no cancellation, rollback or resource cleanup was executed or proved here.

SBCL --no-sysinit/--no-userinit skip initialization files, not core-embedded state. ASDF documents explicit initialization precedence, exactly one inheritance directive, :directory source entries and (t destination) output translation with :implementation components. The two forms are plausible manual DSL examples, explicitly illustrative. ASDF also notes implementation-specific source entries/hardcoded output wrapping and already-defined-system caches, so ignoring inheritance alone is not hermetic proof. Document11 additionally requires clean cores, manifest restrictions, new private outputs and actual resolution/artifact-path checks; pinned-version launcher/CI validation remains phase016.

The eight status values match Document10 Section5 and the existing runtime_operation schema, including cancelled confirmation, rejected-before-execution and stopped_waiting permitting only running/cancel_requested/unknown. CLHS signal/handler behavior and SBCL timeout/termination semantics support separating observed conditions from abnormal completion and waiting from execution. These status labels belong to the framework policy, not a native SBCL status API. Partial-failure consistency and infrastructure diagnostic requirements remain conservative.

Primary manuals provide language and implementation semantics, not controller admission, ownership/lease enforcement, isolation or thirteen-case live evidence. Document11 Sections1/9/11 preserve this boundary and make ASDF forms illustrative. Current Document10 opening and Section12 correctly distinguish delivered schemas/normative binding, optional feature113 adapter capability in phase015, and executable controller/SBCL enforcement/live proofs in phase016115-120. Local2.2.9 availability is only a prior reported availability observation; this preparation did not execute Lisp or independently recapture it.
